name: Pregnancy South Asian
summary: Comforting home cooking from Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Bengal and Pakistan, made for pregnancy: dals and greens, firm egg bhurji, low-mercury fish curries, paneer, roti and gentle breakfasts. Meat, fish and eggs are always cooked through, and the week leaves out the foods Health Canada advises avoiding in pregnancy.
howItWorks:
**Folate and iron, with vitamin C.** Dals, chickpeas, peas and the greens carry your **folate**. Red lentils, moong, goat, sesame and cashews carry the iron, and lemon, tomato, orange and guava sit nearby to help absorb it. Methi is the fresh leaf, cooked as a green, one dish a day at most. Skip fenugreek seed teas and supplements.

**Choline, calcium, iodine and DHA.** Firm egg bhurji, fish, dal and milk bring **choline**. Curd, milk, paneer, sesame and the sardine bones bring calcium. Iodized salt, dairy, eggs and fish carry iodine. Salmon, trout and sardines bring **DHA**, with rohu for a lighter fish day. Rohu is generally low in mercury.

**Gentle mornings.** Poha, moong cheela and a mild bhurji are plain and warm, with ginger and lemon rather than heat. The cheela dal soaks overnight and the poha dal can be cooked the night before. Chai is one cup, twice in the week, well under the caffeine limit.

**Cook once, eat twice, safely.** Dal palak, keema, methi matar paneer and Saturday's dum pulao each make two portions for the next day's lunch. Chill within 1 to 2 hours (rice within 1 hour, spread thin) and reheat once to 74 C, steaming all the way through. Fish dinners are cooked fresh and never kept.

**Other sizes.** Big adds a snack on most days and grows the rice, roti, dal, fish and meat portions. There is no Light size, because a pregnancy plan never goes below 1,800 kcal.

recipes.name: Gentle lemon poha with moong dal, peas and cashews, and a glass of warm milk
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Maharashtrian kanda poha, with moong dal, peas, carrot and cashews and no fried extras
recipes.about: Soft flattened rice tossed with mustard seed, turmeric, a little split moong dal, sweet peas and golden cashews, with just enough lemon to wake up a sleepy appetite. It is mild and easy on a queasy morning. The moong dal and the glass of milk on the side add **protein and calcium**.

ingredients.note: split yellow moong dal, soaked for 30 minutes and drained
seeded, or leave out for a plain morning

steps: Rinse the poha in a sieve under cool running water for about 30 seconds, tossing it with your fingers, then leave it to drain and soften. It should feel tender but still hold its shape.
Warm the oil in a wide pan and add the mustard seed. When it pops, add the cashews and curry leaves and stir for a minute until the cashews are pale gold.
Add the ginger, green chili, onion and carrot and cook for about 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the soaked moong dal, peas and turmeric with 100 ml of water, cover and cook for 8 minutes until the dal and peas are tender.
Fold in the drained poha and the salt and warm through for 2 minutes, stirring gently. Finish with the lemon juice and cilantro.
Warm the milk until it is steaming and serve it alongside.
recipes.tip: On a rushed morning, cook the moong dal and peas the night before and chill them, and the poha takes about 10 minutes. If the smell of onion is too much, leave it out and add a little extra grated carrot.

recipes.name: Firm egg bhurji with tomato and spinach, a warm roti and orange
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi anda bhurji
recipes.about: A homestyle Punjabi scramble with soft onion, ripe tomato and wilted spinach, cooked until the eggs are completely set. Two eggs bring **choline**, and the orange on the side gives vitamin C, which helps with absorbing iron from the roti and the egg.
steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough, knead for a minute, cover and rest while you cook the eggs.
Warm the oil in a pan and add the cumin. When it sizzles, add the onion, ginger and green chili and cook for about 4 minutes until soft.
Add the tomato and turmeric and cook for 4 minutes until the tomato breaks down. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.

Pour in the whisked eggs and stir slowly over medium heat. Keep cooking, breaking up the curds, until the eggs are firm all the way through, with no wet or liquid egg left and the yolk set, 3 to 4 minutes. Scatter over the cilantro.
Roll the dough into 2 small rounds and cook in a hot dry pan for about a minute on each side until they puff and have brown spots. Keep them warm in a clean towel.
Serve the bhurji with the rotis and the orange.

recipes.name: Soft moong dal cheela with spinach and carrot, curd and a banana
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi and Gujarati moong dal cheela
recipes.about: Thin, tender pancakes of ground split moong dal with spinach and grated carrot, cooked until golden and served with cool curd and a ripe banana. It is a mild Gujarati and Punjabi favourite with no chili, so it sits easily in the morning. The dal brings **protein, folate and iron**, and the spinach adds folate.

ingredients.note: split yellow moong dal, soaked for 4 hours or overnight and drained

steps: Blend the soaked dal with the ginger, hing, turmeric, salt and about 100 ml of cold water until completely smooth. The batter should pour like thin pancake batter.
Stir in the spinach, carrot, onion, cumin and cilantro.
Warm a non-stick pan over medium heat and wipe it with a little of the oil. Pour in a ladleful of batter and spread it into a thin round.

Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the underside is golden and the top looks dry, drizzle a little oil around the edge, flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more, until cooked through with no raw batter left. Repeat with the rest.
Serve warm with the curd and the banana.
recipes.tip: Soak the dal in the fridge overnight, and blend the batter fresh in the morning.

recipes.name: Dalia and dal khichdi with cauliflower and ghee, and a bowl of curd
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Gujarati and North Indian dalia khichdi
recipes.about: Cracked wheat, split moong and red lentils cooked together until soft and almost creamy, with cauliflower, carrot and peas and a spoon of ghee. This is the broken-wheat style of khichdi made in Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh, comforting and easy on the stomach. Two kinds of dal bring **protein, folate and iron**, and the curd adds calcium.
steps: Rinse the dalia and both dals together until the water runs mostly clear.
Warm half the ghee in a small pressure cooker or heavy pot and add the cumin and hing. When the cumin sizzles, add the ginger and tomato and cook for 2 minutes.

Add the dalia and dals, cauliflower, carrot, peas, turmeric and salt with about 4 cups of water for every cup of dalia and dal. Pressure cook for 3 whistles, or simmer covered for about 30 minutes, until everything is very soft and porridge-like.
Add a splash of hot water if you like it looser and stir well, mashing the cauliflower in lightly.
Finish with the lemon juice and the rest of the ghee, and serve with the curd.
recipes.tip: The dalia is bulgur or any cracked wheat. For a smoother khichdi, mash it lightly with the back of a spoon.

recipes.name: Chickpea chaat bowl with pomegranate, tamarind and yogurt, and a warm roti
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian chana chaat, with everything cooked and no sprouts
recipes.about: Soft chickpeas tossed with tomato, cucumber, red onion, cilantro, pomegranate and a tangy lemon and tamarind dressing, topped with whisked yogurt the dahi chaat way, and a few crunchy cashews. It is a street-food idea made into a proper lunch, and it works warm or cool. The chickpeas bring **folate, iron and protein**, and the lemon, tomato and pomegranate bring vitamin C along.
steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough and rest it while you make the chaat.
Roast the cashews in a dry pan for 2 to 3 minutes until golden, then crush the cumin seeds in the same hot pan for 30 seconds.

Warm the chickpeas with a splash of water for 3 minutes until steaming, then drain. Wash the tomato, cucumber, onion and cilantro under running water, and the pomegranate arils in a sieve. Cut them and toss with the chickpeas.
Stir the tamarind into the lemon juice with a spoonful of warm water, then dress the chaat with it, the cumin, chaat masala and salt.
Cook the roti in a hot dry pan for about a minute on each side until it puffs. Top the chaat with the yogurt, pomegranate seeds and cashews and serve with the roti.

recipes.name: Pepper sardine fry with a roti and kachumber
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Kerala and Goan sardine fry, made with pantry sardines
recipes.about: Canned sardines folded into a drier onion, ginger and black pepper fry, a quick take on the sardine fries of Kerala and Goa. Mash in the soft bones too: they add **calcium**. Sardines are a low-mercury oily fish, rich in omega-3. Served with a hot roti and a crisp cucumber and tomato kachumber.
steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough, knead briefly and rest it.

Warm the oil and add the mustard seed. When it pops, add the curry leaves and the onion and cook for about 8 minutes until golden at the edges. Stir in the ginger, garlic and green chili for a minute.
Add the ground coriander, turmeric and black pepper and cook for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add a splash of water and the salt, sparingly since the sardines are already salty.
Flake in the sardines and mash the soft bones into the onion. Warm through for 3 minutes and finish with half the lemon and half the cilantro.

Cook the roti in a hot dry pan, about a minute on each side. Wash the cucumber, tomato and the rest of the cilantro under running water, cut them and toss with the rest of the lemon for the kachumber, and serve it all together.
recipes.tip: Canned light or skipjack tuna works if you prefer a milder fish (not albacore or white), but leave out the bones.

recipes.name: Masoor and moong dal palak with a roti and cucumber raita
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi dal palak
recipes.about: A thick, homestyle dal of red lentils and split moong cooked with plenty of spinach and finished with a sizzling cumin, garlic and ghee tadka. The dal brings **iron and protein**, the spinach brings folate, and the lemon at the end helps your body use the iron. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.

ingredients.note: washed and grated, for the raita

steps: Rinse the masoor and moong dal. Cook them with the onion, tomato, ginger, turmeric, salt and about 550 ml of water in a pressure cooker for 3 whistles, or simmer covered for about 30 minutes, until completely soft. Mash lightly.
Stir the spinach into the hot dal and cook for 3 minutes until it wilts and turns deep green.

For the tadka, warm the ghee in a small pan, add the cumin, then the garlic. When the garlic turns golden, take the pan off the heat and add the Kashmiri chili and hing. Pour it over the dal and finish with the lemon and cilantro.
Mix the yogurt with the cucumber and a pinch of salt for the raita. Mix the atta with water into a soft dough and cook the rotis in a hot dry pan.
Eat one portion now. Chill the second portion of dal and raita within 1 to 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat the dal to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through, and make fresh rotis.
recipes.tip: The dal freezes well for a month. Thaw it overnight in the fridge and reheat to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through.

recipes.name: Salmon in a mustard and yogurt curry with cauliflower and rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Bengali shorshe maach, without mustard oil
recipes.about: A Bengali-inspired fish curry: salmon simmered in a sharp, tangy sauce of ground mustard seed, yogurt and green chili with cauliflower and green beans, served over fluffy basmati. Salmon brings **omega-3, DHA and vitamin D**, and it is a low-mercury fish. Cooked fresh and eaten the same day.
steps: Soak the mustard seed in 3 tablespoons of warm water for 10 minutes. Blend it with the green chili, a pinch of salt and a splash of water for just 20 to 30 seconds, then stir in the yogurt. Blending longer makes it bitter.
Cook the rice with twice its volume of water, covered, over low heat for about 30 minutes until tender.

Warm the oil in a wide pan. Add the cauliflower, green beans and turmeric and fry for 5 minutes. Turn the heat to low and stir in the mustard-yogurt mix, the rest of the salt and 150 ml of water. Cover and keep it at a gentle simmer for 8 minutes, until the vegetables are nearly tender. A hard boil will split the yogurt.
Nestle the salmon into the sauce, spoon some over it, cover and cook gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 70 C (158 F).
Finish with the lemon and cilantro and serve over the rice.
recipes.tip: Trout or arctic char work as well as salmon.

recipes.name: Lean goat and fenugreek keema with peas and a roti
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi and Karachi-style keema methi
recipes.about: A Pakistani and Punjabi keema: minced lean goat cooked slowly with onion, tomato, ginger, garam masala, sweet peas and a good handful of fresh fenugreek leaves until fully browned and tender. The goat is a good source of **iron and zinc**, and the tomato and lemon bring vitamin C along. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.

ingredients.note: washed well if fresh, or frozen

steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough, knead briefly and rest it.
Warm the oil in a heavy pan and add the cumin. When it sizzles, add the onion and cook for about 8 minutes until deep golden. Stir in the garlic, ginger and green chili.
Add the minced goat, breaking it up with a spoon, and cook over medium-high heat for 8 minutes until it is browned and no pink is left.

Add the tomato, carrot, ground coriander, turmeric, salt and yogurt and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick. Add the peas, fenugreek leaves and 100 ml of water, cover and simmer for 10 minutes until the meat reaches 71 C (160 F) on a thermometer and is tender.
Stir in the garam masala, lemon and cilantro. Cook the rotis in a hot dry pan and serve.
Chill the second portion within 1 to 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat the keema to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through.
recipes.tip: Lean minced beef works if you cannot find goat. Frozen fenugreek leaves are fine.

recipes.name: Tamarind trout curry with green beans and brown rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tamil meen kuzhambu, with a handful of spinach stirred in
recipes.about: A Tamil-inspired meen kuzhambu: rainbow trout simmered in a tangy tamarind and tomato gravy with curry leaves, shallot-style onion, green beans and a handful of spinach, over brown rice. Trout brings **omega-3, DHA and vitamin D** and is a low-mercury fish. Tamarind adds the sour that makes South Indian curries taste bright.

ingredients.note: trimmed and cut in short lengths
untoasted (gingelly), not the dark toasted kind

steps: Cook the brown rice with twice its volume of water, covered, over low heat for about 30 minutes until tender.
Warm the sesame oil in a wide pan. Add the mustard seed. When it pops, add the curry leaves, onion and garlic and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the green beans and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the tomato, ground coriander, Kashmiri chili, turmeric and salt and cook for 5 minutes until the tomato breaks down.
Dissolve the tamarind in 250 ml of hot water, pour it in and simmer for 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach.
Slide in the trout, cover and cook gently for 8 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily, and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 70 C (158 F). Do not stir hard.
Scatter with the cilantro and serve over the rice.

recipes.name: Methi matar paneer in a tomato-cashew gravy with a roti
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi methi matar paneer
recipes.about: Cubes of paneer, sweet green peas and a few chickpeas in a smooth tomato gravy thickened with a little cashew, with fresh fenugreek leaves stirred in. Buy paneer that says it is made from pasteurised milk on the label, and simmer it until steaming, as the recipe does. The paneer brings **calcium and protein**, the peas and chickpeas bring folate, and the tomato gives vitamin C. The fenugreek is the fresh leaf, cooked as a green. Makes two portions, so tomorrow's lunch is done.

ingredients.note: washed well if fresh, or frozen

steps: Mix the atta with warm water into a soft dough, knead briefly and rest it. Soak the cashews in hot water for 10 minutes.
Warm the oil and add the cumin. Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for 8 minutes until golden. Add the tomato, Kashmiri chili, turmeric and salt and cook for 8 minutes until soft and jammy.
Let the mixture cool for a few minutes, then blend it with the drained cashews and a splash of water until completely smooth.
Return the gravy to the pan with 100 ml of water. Add the peas, chickpeas and fenugreek leaves and simmer for 6 minutes. Add the paneer, garam masala and kasuri methi and simmer for 4 minutes.
Top with the cilantro. Cook the rotis in a hot dry pan and serve.
Chill the second portion within 1 to 2 hours. Tomorrow, reheat the curry to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through.

recipes.name: Chicken and vegetable dum pulao with cucumber raita
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Hyderabadi and Pakistani dum pulao
recipes.about: A weekend one-pot pulao: chicken marinated in yogurt and ginger, layered over half-cooked basmati with peas, saffron, fried onion and cashews, then sealed and steamed on low heat until fragrant. It is a Hyderabadi and Pakistani celebration idea made lighter with brown basmati. The chicken is cooked all the way through. Makes two portions for tomorrow's lunch.

ingredients.note: plain, pasteurised, half for the raita
a pinch, soaked in warm water
washed and grated, for the raita

steps: Marinate the chicken with half the yogurt, the ginger, garlic, green chili, garam masala and half the salt for at least 30 minutes in the fridge, and up to 4 hours. Wash your hands, board and knife after handling the raw chicken.

Warm the oil in a heavy pot and fry the cashews for a minute until pale gold, then lift them out. Fry the onion in the same oil over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown. Take out half for the top.
Add the chicken with its marinade to the pot and cook for 12 minutes, stirring now and then. Add the peas.
Meanwhile boil the rice in plenty of water with the bay leaf and clove for 22 minutes until about three-quarters cooked, then drain.

Spread the rice over the chicken. Top with the reserved onion, the cashews, the cilantro, the lemon and the saffron with its soaking liquid. Cover tightly with foil and the lid and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes. The chicken must reach 74 C (165 F) on a thermometer, with clear juices.
Stir the rest of the yogurt with the cucumber and a pinch of salt for the raita. Rest the pulao for 5 minutes, then fluff and serve.

Chill the second portion of pulao and raita within 1 hour, spread thin in a shallow dish so the rice cools quickly. Eat both by tomorrow's lunch, and reheat the pulao only once, to 74 C (165 F), steaming all the way through.
recipes.tip: Cooked rice must cool fast: spread it thin, chill within 1 hour, eat it by the next day and reheat it only once.

recipes.name: Bengali-style rohu jhol with cauliflower, green beans, spinach and rice
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Bengali maacher jhol, with a three-seed tempering in place of panch phoron
recipes.about: A light, golden fish stew of rohu, the freshwater carp Bengali homes cook most weeks, with cauliflower, green beans and spinach in a thin ginger and cumin gravy. It is a soothing, brothy dish, like a Sunday lunch, and a fish that is generally low in mercury. It brings lean protein and **B12**. Cooked fresh.

ingredients.note: steaks, or fillets if you can get them

steps: Pat the rohu dry and rub it with a little turmeric and half the salt. Cook the rice with twice its volume of water, covered, over low heat for about 30 minutes.
Warm half the oil in a wide pan and sear the fish for 2 minutes a side, just to firm it. Lift it out onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan and the cumin, fennel and mustard. When they sizzle, add the ginger, green chili and tomato and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the cauliflower, green beans, remaining turmeric and salt and 400 ml of water. Cover and simmer for 12 minutes until the vegetables are tender. Stir in the spinach.

Lay the fish in the stew and simmer gently for 8 minutes, until it is opaque and flakes easily, and a thermometer in the thickest part reads 70 C (158 F). Finish with the lemon and cilantro and serve with the rice.
recipes.tip: Frozen rohu from an Indian or Bangladeshi grocer is common. Thaw it in the fridge and cook it the same day. Rohu has fine bones, so take your time with it. Cod works if you cannot find it.

recipes.name: Guava, orange and pomegranate fruit chaat
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Delhi phal chaat
recipes.about: Juicy guava, orange segments and pomegranate seeds with lemon and a pinch of chaat masala, the classic street-side fruit plate. It gives a big hit of **vitamin C**, which goes well with the iron in the meals around it.

ingredients.note: washed and cubed, seeds and all

steps: Scrub the guava and orange under running water, then cut the guava into cubes and segment the orange. Rinse the pomegranate seeds in a sieve.
Toss with the pomegranate seeds, lemon juice and chaat masala just before eating.

recipes.name: Cardamom and ginger masala chai with almonds
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian masala chai
recipes.about: A cup of milky chai with fresh ginger, cardamom and a little jaggery, with a small handful of almonds on the side. One cup is well under Health Canada's 300 mg a day caffeine limit for pregnancy, so just count it along with any other tea, coffee or cola that day. Have it between meals rather than with the iron-rich ones. The almonds bring **vitamin E**.

ingredients.note: black tea bag and its water

steps: Put the water for the tea in a small pan with the ginger and cardamom and simmer for 2 minutes, until it smells warm and spicy.
Add the tea bag and simmer for 2 minutes more, until it is a deep amber. Pour in the milk and jaggery and bring it just up to the boil.
Strain into a cup and serve with the almonds.

recipes.name: Carrot and cucumber raita with cashews
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian vegetable raita
recipes.about: Cool yogurt with grated carrot, cucumber, roasted cumin and a few crushed roasted cashews. A light, crunchy raita to eat from a bowl, with **protein, calcium and beta-carotene** from the carrot.
steps: Dry-roast the cashews in a pan until pale gold, then crush them. Crush the cumin seeds in the same hot pan.
Whisk the yogurt until smooth and stir in the carrot, cucumber, cumin and salt.
Top with the cashews and cilantro.

recipes.name: Banana and cardamom lassi
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi lassi
recipes.about: Ripe banana blended with cold yogurt and a pinch of cardamom. Store-bought yogurt or dahi you set at home from pasteurised milk both work. It brings **calcium and potassium**, and it is a cooling snack.
steps: Blend the banana, yogurt, cardamom and a splash of cold water until smooth.
Serve cold right away.

recipes.name: Masoor dal shorba in a mug
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian dal ka shorba
recipes.about: A thin, warm, lemony soup of red lentils with tomato, ginger and cumin, sipped from a mug between meals. Red lentils are a good source of **iron, folate and protein**, and the lemon helps with absorbing that iron.
steps: Simmer the lentils with the tomato, ginger, turmeric, salt and 350 ml of water for about 20 minutes, until completely soft. Blend or mash until smooth.
Warm the ghee in a small pan, crackle the cumin for 20 seconds and pour it into the soup.
Finish with the lemon and cilantro and pour into a mug. Eat it hot.

recipes.name: Chickpea sundal with curry leaves and lemon
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Tamil sundal
recipes.about: Chickpeas tossed in a quick tempering of mustard seed, curry leaves and green chili with a squeeze of lemon, the South Indian temple snack. A fibre-rich snack with **folate and protein**.
steps: Warm the oil and add the mustard seed. When it pops, add the curry leaves, green chili and hing.
Add the chickpeas and warm them through for 3 minutes until steaming hot.
Turn off the heat and add the lemon juice.

recipes.name: Banana with almonds and cardamom
recipes.about: A ripe banana sliced with a handful of almonds and a pinch of cardamom. Plain, quick and gentle on the stomach, with **potassium and vitamin B6**.
steps: Slice the banana and top with the almonds and cardamom.

recipes.name: Pomegranate raita bowl with roasted cumin and almonds
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by pomegranate raita
recipes.about: Cool yogurt with ruby pomegranate seeds, roasted cumin, slivered almonds and a pinch of salt. A refreshing, light snack with **calcium, vitamin C and vitamin E**.
steps: Whisk the yogurt until smooth and stir in the cumin and salt.
Rinse the pomegranate seeds in a sieve.
Top the yogurt with the pomegranate seeds and almonds.

recipes.name: Sesame, cashew and jaggery ladoo
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian til ladoo
recipes.about: Toasted sesame seeds and cashews pounded with jaggery and cardamom into little balls, a winter staple in many North Indian homes. Sesame brings **iron, calcium and zinc**.
steps: Dry-roast the sesame seeds and cashews separately in a pan over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until pale golden and fragrant.
Grind them coarsely with the cardamom. Melt the jaggery with a spoon of water until it bubbles, about 2 minutes, then stir in the ground mix.
Let it cool for a minute until you can handle it, then press into two tight balls with damp hands while it is still warm.

recipes.name: Spiced cumin chaas
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by North Indian chaas
recipes.about: A tall glass of cold, thin, salty-sour yogurt drink with roasted cumin, the traditional cooling drink with a meal. It is a source of **calcium and protein**.
steps: Whisk the yogurt with 200 ml of cold water, the cumin and the salt until frothy.
Serve cold.

recipes.name: Warm almond and cardamom milk
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by badam doodh
recipes.about: A mug of warm milk with a few almonds ground in and a pinch of cardamom, a comforting evening drink in many homes. It brings **calcium, protein and vitamin E**.
steps: Warm the milk with the ground almonds and cardamom until steaming, about 5 minutes, stirring so it does not catch.
Stir in the jaggery and pour into a mug.

recipes.name: Guava with lemon and chaat masala
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by amrood chaat
recipes.about: Ripe guava cut into wedges with lemon and a pinch of chaat masala. A simple street-side snack that is very high in **vitamin C** and fibre.

ingredients.note: washed, in wedges, seeds and all

steps: Wash the guava well and cut it into wedges.
Squeeze over the lemon and sprinkle with the chaat masala.

recipes.name: Saffron and cardamom lassi
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Punjabi lassi
recipes.about: Cold yogurt whisked with a few saffron threads, cardamom and a little jaggery, a gently sweet lassi. Store-bought yogurt or dahi you set at home from pasteurised milk both work. It brings **calcium and protein**.

ingredients.note: a few threads, soaked in a spoon of warm water

steps: Soak the saffron in a spoonful of warm water for 5 minutes.
Whisk the yogurt with the saffron water, cardamom, jaggery and a splash of cold water until smooth and serve cold.

recipes.name: Pepper sardines with cucumber and lemon
recipes.inspiredBy: Inspired by Kerala sardine fry, served cold
recipes.about: Canned sardines with sliced cucumber, a squeeze of lemon, black pepper and cilantro, a quick no-cook plate. Mash in the soft bones too: they add **calcium**. A low-mercury oily fish with omega-3 and **choline**.
steps: Drain the sardines and lay them on a plate with the sliced cucumber.
Squeeze over the lemon and finish with the black pepper and cilantro.
Mash a few of the soft bones into the fish as you eat.
